title: Saved boundaries and transient reconstruction
question: When can a reconstructed activation be freed?
scope: Toy two-layer segment after forward completion. Activation slots have equal schematic size; weights, gradients, RNG replay, and other segments are outside this view. a0 remains needed upstream.

steps.title: Start after the forward segment
steps.explanation: Only selected boundaries were retained; a1 is absent.

snapshot.result: The backward pass will need an activation that is no longer resident.

steps.title: Recompute a1 from retained a0
steps.explanation: Evaluate the missing internal activation from the saved boundary. The read leaves a0 intact.

snapshot.result: Reconstructed a1 occupies transient memory until its backward consumer finishes.

transition.meaning: Evaluate the missing internal activation from the saved boundary. The read leaves a0 intact.

steps.title: Execute backward for layer 2
steps.explanation: Layer 2 reads a1 and the retained output boundary a2 to produce its gradient.

snapshot.result: a1 remains live because the next backward operation still consumes it.

transition.meaning: Layer 2 reads a1 and the retained output boundary a2 to produce its gradient.

steps.title: Release checkpoint a2
steps.explanation: Its final backward consumer has finished.

snapshot.result: Releasing a2 frees a slot; a0 and a1 remain resident.

transition.meaning: Its final backward consumer has finished.

steps.title: Execute backward for layer 1
steps.explanation: The final operation in this segment consumes a0 and reconstructed a1.

snapshot.result: Both segment backward operations have finished.

transition.meaning: The final operation in this segment consumes a0 and reconstructed a1.

steps.title: Release reconstructed a1
steps.explanation: No backward consumer in this segment needs a1 again.

snapshot.result: The temporary slot is free; the earlier checkpoint a0 remains for upstream work.

transition.meaning: No backward consumer in this segment needs a1 again.

invariants: A checkpoint read does not remove its saved activation.
Reconstructed a1 remains resident through its final backward consumer.
The toy counts show this segment’s activation lifetime, not a universal memory-saving ratio.

title: Prefetch into a separate buffer

steps.title: Begin filling the first reserved buffer
steps.explanation: Each batch must finish host open/read before its GPU training can begin.

snapshot.result: Two slots bound prefetch capacity; a GPU consumer keeps its buffer occupied.

steps.title: Complete Fill A
steps.explanation: The producer fills a separate buffer.

snapshot.result: Data ownership and task readiness agree at this boundary.

transition.meaning: The producer fills a separate buffer.

steps.title: Complete Fill B
steps.explanation: The producer fills a separate buffer.

snapshot.result: The next batch may become ready while GPU training still uses the other slot.

transition.meaning: The producer fills a separate buffer.

steps.title: Complete Train A
steps.explanation: Training consumes this batch and releases its buffer only at completion.

snapshot.result: Data ownership and task readiness agree at this boundary.

transition.meaning: Training consumes this batch and releases its buffer only at completion.

steps.title: Complete Train B
steps.explanation: Training consumes this batch and releases its buffer only at completion.

snapshot.result: All training is complete.

Host and GPU each run at most one task at a time; their tasks may overlap.

steps.explanation: The fixed selection keeps A, C, and E.

title: Range selection allocates finite codes
question: How does a narrower calibration range trade rounding for clipping?
scope: Four fixed toy samples share signed codes −2, −1, 0, and 1. Symmetric mapping uses −1, 0, and 1 with zero point 0; code −2 is reserved for equal-magnitude endpoints. Asymmetric mappings use all four codes with zero point −1. This toy code width differs from printed INT8 and does not measure model accuracy.

steps.title: Fix samples and a four-code budget
steps.explanation: All three mappings use the same observations and integer code storage.

snapshot.result: Changing calibration changes represented real values, not the source samples.

steps.title: Symmetric: scale 1.5, zero point 0
steps.explanation: Apply the declared affine map q = clamp(round(x/scale) + zero point). Original samples remain fixed.

snapshot.result: Real zero maps to integer zero; the most negative code is reserved to retain equal-magnitude endpoints.

transition.meaning: Apply the declared affine map q = clamp(round(x/scale) + zero point). Original samples remain fixed.

steps.title: Asymmetric: scale 0.75, zero point −1
steps.explanation: Apply the declared affine map q = clamp(round(x/scale) + zero point). Original samples remain fixed.

snapshot.result: The skewed range assigns more usable levels to these observations.

transition.meaning: Apply the declared affine map q = clamp(round(x/scale) + zero point). Original samples remain fixed.

steps.title: Narrow range: scale 0.25, zero point −1
steps.explanation: Apply the declared affine map q = clamp(round(x/scale) + zero point). Original samples remain fixed.

snapshot.result: The narrower grid improves spacing but clips the high samples.

transition.meaning: Apply the declared affine map q = clamp(round(x/scale) + zero point). Original samples remain fixed.

invariants: The calibration observations remain unchanged in every state.
Each active level reconstructs as scale × (code − zero point).
Clipping counts source samples outside the represented endpoint interval.
Reconstruction error on these samples does not establish model accuracy.

title: Codes, wide sums, and the output conversion

steps.explanation: Scales and zero points define how integer codes represent the floating-point operands.
